name: jidec-l2-shape-template
producer: SYNTHETIC -- the jidec-chain-v1 wire shape extended to L2 (not the JIDEC ledger, not endorsed by its maintainer)
description: Template for the L2 loss-accounting walk of vlc-1 issue #12. Same chain recipe as jidec-ledger-chained; three additions, none of which changes any existing entry hash because sha256-canonical-fields omits absent fields: submission_seq on event entries (producer intake ordinal), a jidec-loss-v1 declaration class with {lost, from_seq, to_seq}, and produced_count on the BOUND end marker (EXT-022: read from the bound marker, the count cannot be lowered after the fact). Identity: delivered + declared == produced_count. See README.md and build_and_check.py beside this file.

integrity.note: Same recipe as the live adapter; the five new fields join hash_fields so the declarations are bound, and their absence from historical entries leaves those hashes unchanged.

loss.note: produced_count is the producer-side figure over the submission_seq window since genesis (cumulative). Per-day windows are the lighter operational trade; the field and identity are the same either way. A declaration states count AND interval (VLC-L2-2), and the checker cross-checks declared intervals against delivered submission_seq values.

coverage.note: The ledger records what submitters and the operator's schedule send it (witness batches, specifications, datasets). It does not enumerate what it was supposed to receive; a submission that never arrived leaves no trace.

policy.note: Acceptance rules live in the worker's source, not in the entries. An entry does not bind the intake rules that admitted it.

independence.boundary_statement: The ledger is operated by the same company whose specifications, datasets and gate measurements appear in it, and the operator holds the write token. Witness batches bundle walks written by third parties, but the batch entry itself is written by the operator's worker. The Bitcoin anchor is external; the ledger is not.
